record.paper_title: Exact results and open questions in first principle functional RG
record.original_question: How can the functional renormalization-group treatment of disordered elastic manifolds control the physics of multiple metastable minima and quasi-degenerate states in a systematic way, given that the proliferation of minima makes the problem appear intrinsically non-perturbative?

evidence.quote: It is true however that handling multiple minima intuitively appear as a non perturbative problem, so it remains to be understood precisely how it can ever be controlled.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a $d$-dimensional elastic manifold parameterized by a displacement field $u:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^N$ embedded in a quenched random potential $V(u,x)$, with replicated effective action whose disorder part is encoded in a renormalized correlator $R(u)$ of the random potential. The Wilsonian functional renormalization-group (FRG) flow of $R(u)$ near $d=4$ generically develops a non-analytic "cusp" at a finite RG scale, signaling the onset of many quasi-degenerate metastable minima of the pinning energy landscape (so-called shocks/avalanches). The proliferation of these metastable minima and quasi-degenerate ground states makes a naive perturbative treatment around a single minimum break down and appears intrinsically non-perturbative.

Problem. Develop a systematic and controlled framework, within first-principles functional renormalization group for disordered elastic manifolds, that captures and accounts for the physics of multiple metastable minima and quasi-degenerate states. Specifically:

(a) Formulate an FRG scheme (e.g., based on the effective action $\Gamma[u]$, its higher replica cumulants $S^{(p)}(u_1,\dots,u_p)$ for $p\ge 2$, or a suitable resummation of the cusp singularity) in which the contributions from configurations sitting in different near-degenerate minima are organized into a small parameter and can be incorporated order by order.

(b) Prove that such a scheme correctly reproduces, in appropriate limits, both the perturbative $\varepsilon=4-d$ expansion of Balents–Fisher–Le Doussal–Wiese and the large-$N$ mean-field/replica-symmetry-breaking results, and that it remains finite and predictive at and beyond the Larkin scale where multiple minima first appear.

(c) Quantify, within this scheme, observable consequences of multiple minima — in particular shock/avalanche statistics, the second cumulant cusp and third cumulant anomaly, droplet exponents, and chaos in temperature and disorder — with rigorous error control.

State whether such a controlled FRG treatment of multiple minima exists and, if so, exhibit it; otherwise, identify the obstruction.
artifact.category_tag: Functional renormalization group for disordered systems
artifact.status_search_result: The question of how to systematically control the FRG when many metastable minima proliferate remains an active research area. Subsequent work (large-N FRG and its connection to replica symmetry breaking, droplet/shock and avalanche analyses, and nonperturbative FRG benchmarks such as the 2019 study of the random elastic manifold model) has made substantial progress in incorporating multiple-minima effects, but no fully controlled, all-order systematic scheme has been established. The problem is generally regarded as partially addressed but still open in its strongest form.

status_evidence.title: Functional renormalization group at large N for disordered elastic systems, and relation to replica symmetry breaking
status_evidence.snippet: Computes the full effective action exactly at large N and derives an FRG equation valid in any dimension, relating the cusp to replica symmetry breaking and metastability.
status_evidence.claim: Large-N FRG provides a controlled handle on multiple minima via RSB connection, but only in the large-N limit.

status_evidence.title: Benchmarking the nonperturbative functional renormalization group approach on the random elastic manifold model in and out of equilibrium
status_evidence.snippet: Applies nonperturbative FRG to disordered elastic manifolds and benchmarks against known results.
status_evidence.claim: As of 2019, controlling multiple minima within FRG is still an active investigation rather than a settled result.

status_evidence.title: Chaos in the thermal regime for pinned manifolds via functional RG
status_evidence.snippet: Uses FRG with cusp/boundary-layer analysis to study chaos and thermal effects.
status_evidence.claim: Boundary-layer/thermal regularization controls some multiple-minima physics, but a fully systematic scheme remains incomplete.
